recommendations.title: Flood-proof the grid where flood claims concentrate
recommendations.evidence: ZIPs with the longest outages had 4.5× the flood-claim rate of the fastest-restored ZIPs (45 vs 10 claims per 1,000 customers; rank correlation +0.40, 198 ZIPs).
recommendations.action: Elevate or flood-harden substations and pad-mounted equipment in the hotspot ZIPs, and pre-stage mobile generation on high ground beside them before landfall.
recommendations.target_places: Porter, Kingwood, Energy Corridor, Montgomery, Conroe, Braeswood and 17 more
recommendations.target_rule: Slowest-restored quarter of ZIPs (at least 0.25 days out per customer) that are also in the top quarter for flood claims (at least 35 per 1,000 customers).

recommendations.title: Start with the named hotspots
recommendations.evidence: The longest outages clustered in Porter (77365), Huffman (77336), Kingwood (77339), Kingwood (77345), Lake Houston area (77044), Sheldon (77049).
recommendations.action: Make these the first areas for hardening, pre-staged crews and mobile generation, and keep relief supplies on high ground inside each cluster.
recommendations.target_places: Porter, Kingwood, Lake Houston area, Sheldon, Huffman
recommendations.target_rule: The three hotspot clusters: slowest-quarter ZIPs within 8 km of each other, ranked by median outage length.

recommendations.title: Clear roads and restore information first
recommendations.evidence: Distance to a service center did not separate long and short outages (rank correlation 0.06). Reports point to blocked roads and missing outage information instead.
recommendations.action: Pair crew staging with debris-clearing crews on access routes, and keep a working outage map and call line from hour one.
recommendations.target_places: Spring, Downtown Houston, Gulfton, Galveston, Beasley, Fifth Ward and 6 more
recommendations.target_rule: Slowest-restored quarter of ZIPs with below-median flood claims (under 17 per 1,000 customers). These are access-review candidates; the data does not identify blocked roads or establish the cause of each outage.

recommendations.title: Segment circuits serving smaller and outlying areas
recommendations.evidence: Smaller ZIPs ran slightly longer outages (rank correlation -0.10 with customer count), as the PUCT found for less-populated areas and single-line service.
recommendations.action: Add sectionalizers and automatic reclosers so one fault no longer darkens a whole outlying feeder.
recommendations.target_places: Porter, Montgomery, Conroe, Angleton, The Woodlands, Beasley and 11 more
recommendations.target_rule: Smaller ZIPs (bottom quarter, up to 6,732 customers) more than 25 km from downtown Houston with slower-than-median restoration.

recommendations.title: For wind storms like Beryl, target trees
recommendations.strength: Supported by 3 reports; ZIP data to confirm
recommendations.evidence: CenterPoint found its longest Beryl outages where rainfall and vegetation were highest, and the PUCT found most tree damage came from outside utility rights-of-way.
recommendations.action: Create a way for residents to report hazard trees, trim beyond rights-of-way with owner consent, and collect circuit-level canopy data so the next storm can be measured ZIP by ZIP.
recommendations.target_places: Harris (74 hours), Galveston (68 hours), Montgomery (65 hours)
recommendations.target_rule: Counties that took at least the median 65 hours to halve Beryl outages (EAGLE-I). Beryl outage data exists only by county.
